title: Math utilities, noise and spatial fields
summary: Use vectors, matrices, noise and spatial fields to describe motion and procedural geometry.

blocks.text: Vec2/Vec3, Point, Quaternion, Mat3/Mat4 and AABB provide engine-native mathematics and typed-array views. Some operations mutate and return the receiver while others produce a new object. Read the specific method contract before reusing a scratch vector. Singular matrix inversion and zero quaternion inversion are explicit failure cases.

FourierTransform computes discrete Fourier coefficients for sampled 2D complex coordinates and supports epicycle reconstruction. Sample a path consistently, choose coefficient ordering intentionally and balance truncation against visible detail. A finite set of coefficients approximates the source, with ringing and sampling artifacts near sharp corners.

The math/noise directory contains seeded procedural noise implementations and utilities. Choose a generator based on its dimensionality, continuity, repeatability and output range. A seed stabilizes the noise field; the sampling coordinate determines whether it stays attached to local geometry or moves through world space.

Noise used for static geometry should remain in the same coordinate system across frames. For motion, animate a coordinate/phase smoothly instead of selecting a new unrelated random field every frame.
All noise classes and their exact sample/seed methods appear in the math/noise API.

The fields subsystem constructs deformation functions for geometry and animation. Apply maps in a documented order; function composition is generally non-commutative. Track whether a function returns an absolute point or a displacement. A custom mapping must preserve finite coordinates and receive adequate subdivision to show curvature.
One seeded Perlin source is sampled as one scalar curve.
